claim: A model-level backdoor audit of CLIP classifiers still works against an attacker who deliberately narrows the trigger so that only the exact pattern fires, and against backdoors planted in a fine-tuned image encoder instead of a prompt-tuning module. A backdoor counts as caught only when the model's anomaly score reaches 2 and the audit's recovered trigger achieves at least 50% attack success. Supported only if the audit catches a majority of the narrowed-trigger backdoors and every encoder-level backdoor tested.

experiments: Assemble clean and backdoored models to audit. Setup: CLIP ViT-B/16 prompt-tuned with CoCoOp (encoders frozen) on the seen classes of ten datasets (ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, Flowers102, Food101, FGVC Aircraft, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, UCF101); per dataset one clean model and four backdoored ones (BadCLIP, plus Blended, SIBA and WaNet adapted to prompt tuning, 10% poisoning), 50 models in all. Result: backdoored models keep clean accuracy close to the clean models (about 82% seen-class) with high attack success (BadCLIP about 99% seen, 97% unseen; SIBA weakest at about 66%/52%).

Detection against an attacker who knows the audit. Setup: a two-phase BadCLIP variant that first learns a trigger, then trains the model to fire only on that exact trigger and to ignore noisy approximations of it, which is what inversion recovers. Result: the attack itself weakens (seen-class success about 64% instead of 99%); recovered triggers drop to about 70% success; the audit still flags 8 of 10 adaptive models, missing EuroSAT (anomaly score 1.66, under 2) and UCF101 (recovered trigger only 31% successful, treated as invalid).

Does the audit find backdoors outside the prompt module? Setup: fully fine-tune CLIP's image encoder with Blended poisoning (no prompt module at all) using three trigger patterns (noise patch, triangle, text) and run the audit unchanged. Result: all three poisoned models are flagged, with anomaly scores 6.15, 5.93 and 4.38 and recovered triggers reaching 99%, 97% and 62% attack success.
